subject: religious-studies
title: Wittgenstein, Analogy and Symbol
welcome_lead: Cross from logical positivism to the later Wittgenstein, then back to Aquinas's analogy and Tillich's symbol, surveying the toolbox of religious language.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on Wittgensteinian language games, Aquinas on analogy, and Tillich on religious symbol.
final_note: You have surveyed three rival models of how religious language signifies.

walkthroughs.h2: Language Games and Forms of Life
walkthroughs.body_html: Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations (1953) abandons the picture theory of the Tractatus. 'The meaning of a word is its use in the language.' Religious utterance is a distinctive language game, with its own rules, embedded in the form of life of a believing community. D. Z. Phillips developed this into a 'Wittgensteinian fideism', insisting that the believer's prayer should not be assessed by physicists' standards.

If 'God is good' were univocal with 'Socrates is good', divine transcendence would collapse; if equivocal, theology would say nothing. Aquinas (ST I, Q.13) proposes analogy. By attribution, creaturely goodness derives from God; by proportion, each thing is good in the mode of its own being. Analogy preserves both the reality and the mystery of theological speech.

Paul Tillich, in Dynamics of Faith (1957), distinguishes sign from symbol. A sign points away from itself; a symbol participates in what it signifies. 'God' is the highest symbol for Being-Itself. Symbols 'open up levels of reality which otherwise are closed to us'. They are born and die in the life of a culture. The only non-symbolic statement, Tillich says, is that God is being-itself.

mcqs.q: What are James's four characteristics of mystical experience?
options: Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Ineffability (beyond words), noetic quality (gives knowledge), transience (temporary), and passivity (feeling acted upon by something greater).
Religious experiences are just hallucinations caused by stress.
Religious experiences only happen during dreams.

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological argument try to prove?
options: That the existence of the universe requires a first cause or necessary being — usually identified with God — to explain why anything exists at all.
The cosmological argument proves who created life on Earth.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
The cosmological argument proves the Big Bang happened.
